tasks.short: Work out where Noordhaven stands financially now and over the next quarters, from AFAS and forecast data.

today.trigger: Month close, the quarterly reforecast, or a board or bank question about results and cash.
steps: Pull the general ledger, open items and the Power BI extract from AFAS into Excel
Match the actuals against the budget and the FP&A forecast per site and per value stream
Adjust for known events: CAO wage step, flex-worker peak, fuel price, large customer wins or losses
Write a short view of margin, cash and covenant headroom for the director team
drudgery: Re-linking Excel sheets to a fresh AFAS export each month
Explaining the same variances again in every meeting
today.time_sinks: Collecting and reconciling numbers from AFAS, agency invoices and the bank before any analysis can start.

lenses.faster: The data pull, the variance tables and the first draft of commentary come ready from a fixed Power BI model with a model-written explanation; the director spends the time on the three or four variances that matter, about a third less time overall.
lenses.autonomous: The nightly AFAS refresh after close starts a variance pack and draft commentary; nothing goes to the board or bank until the director has read and signed it.
lenses.ambitious: A decision made far more often: a rolling 13-week cash and margin view every week instead of a quarterly reforecast, which the operations managers in Rotterdam, Tilburg and Venlo would use more as it gets cheaper.
lenses.joy: Nobody misses re-linking spreadsheets; the director wants more time judging which customers and sites carry the risk.
lenses.options: Two or three forecast scenarios (flex-worker peak high or low, fuel up or down) change the call on hiring freezes and facility drawdown, not just the effort.
lenses.altitude: The week shifts from building the numbers to challenging them with site managers; the director gains the right to set the forecast method and the variance thresholds, and the work becomes more expert.
reach: Absorb part of the FP&A Analyst's monthly reforecast build; needs comfort with the Power BI data model and driver-based forecasting

tasks.human_edge: Knowing which customer is about to leave, which site manager sandbags, and what the bank and board will read into a number; that context is not in AFAS.
tasks.pattern_why: The director stays the lead; AI assembles data and drafts explanations, but the view of future status is a judgment the director signs.

in_practice.trigger: Nightly AFAS extract after the month-close cut-off, or a weekly cash run.
steps: Power BI model refreshes actuals, budget and forecast per site
Model call drafts variance commentary from the variance table and known events list
Director reviews, edits and adds forward view
Signed pack saved to SharePoint and sent to the director team
in_practice.human_gate: Director approves every forward-looking statement before it leaves finance.
systems: approved company AI assistant in Microsoft 365
in_practice.logs_to: SharePoint finance pack folder with version history and the prompt and source extract used.

evidence.claim: Faster reporting tends to produce more reports; AI-mature teams spend more hours on executive reporting, not fewer.
Only 12% of Dutch finance professionals plan cash-in more than 30 days ahead.
A model can draft variance commentary from a structured variance table.

risks: Forecast figures pasted into personal chatbots instead of an approved tool
Commentary that sounds sure but rests on a wrong AFAS mapping
More packs produced, eating the saved time
research_questions: How many hours a month does the director spend gathering versus analysing, measured over two closes?
Is the Power BI extract clean enough per site and cost centre to drive variance commentary without manual fixes?
Would site managers act on a weekly 13-week view, or ignore it?

tasks.short: Decide credit limits for new and growing shipper customers, and handle bank facility requests.

today.trigger: Sales asks for a credit limit for a new or growing customer, or the bank facility is up for renewal.
steps: Look up the customer at KvK and in the credit agency report
Check payment history and open items in AFAS
Weigh expected volume against risk and set a limit or ask for security
Record the limit in AFAS and tell sales and the Credit and Collections Officer
drudgery: Copying KvK and credit report figures into a template
today.time_sinks: Collecting the same basic data for each request, often under time pressure from sales.

lenses.faster: The data collection and a proposal with reasons arrive as one file; the director reads, adjusts and approves in minutes instead of half an hour, about 45% saved.
lenses.autonomous: A credit request form in Teams or AFAS starts a pull of KvK, credit score and AFAS payment history and a proposed limit; the limit only counts once the director or, under a threshold, the Credit and Collections Officer approves.
lenses.ambitious: A decision made far more often: review every customer limit each quarter against actual payment behaviour, not only at onboarding, and demand would grow as it gets cheaper.
lenses.joy: Nobody misses retyping credit reports; the director wants more time on the few large customers where a limit shapes the commercial deal.
lenses.options: Two or three limit options (lower limit, limit with guarantee, shorter terms) change what sales offers the customer.
lenses.altitude: The director moves from approving each limit to setting the credit policy, thresholds and delegation table, and audits a sample; the work becomes more expert.
reach: Absorb first-line limit proposals from the Credit and Collections Officer; needs to own the scoring rules and the AI Act check for sole traders

tasks.human_edge: Reading the commercial relationship, a customer's sector trouble, and the bank's mood; and taking accountability for a credit loss.
tasks.pattern_why: One model call turns KvK data, a credit report and AFAS history into a checkable proposal inside a fixed request workflow.

in_practice.trigger: Credit limit request submitted by sales.
steps: Fetch KvK extract, credit score and AFAS payment history
Model drafts proposed limit, terms and reasons against the credit policy
Flag sole traders (natural persons) for human-only assessment
Approver accepts or changes; limit written to AFAS
in_practice.human_gate: Every limit approved by a person; above the delegated threshold only the director.
data_needed: AFAS payment history and open items
in_practice.logs_to: AFAS customer card note plus a SharePoint credit decision log with inputs, proposal and approver.

evidence.claim: Creditworthiness scoring of natural persons is a high-risk AI use under Annex III 5(b); sole-trader hauliers and small shippers can be natural persons.
Advisors recommend mandatory human review and timestamped logs for credit and cash allocation decisions.

risks: Using a model to score sole traders falls under EU AI Act high-risk duties
Credit data shared outside the approved tool, an AVG/GDPR issue
research_questions: How many limit requests a month, and how many are sole traders?
Does the credit agency contract allow its data to be passed to an AI model?
Would quarterly re-reviews have caught last year's bad debts earlier?

tasks.short: Go through the debtor ageing and collection reports to see who owes what and where to push.

today.trigger: Weekly ageing review and the month-end DSO number.
steps: Run the open items report in AFAS
Sort by age and amount in Excel
Discuss the top overdue customers with the Credit and Collections Officer
Decide on escalation, stop-supply or provision
drudgery: Rebuilding the same ageing sheet each week
Reading notes spread over e-mails to know a dispute's status
today.time_sinks: Finding the reason behind each overdue balance: a dispute, a missing POD, or just slow payment.

lenses.faster: An ageing dashboard and a ranked exception list with dispute status come ready each Monday; the director reviews only the exceptions, cutting about 60% of the time.
lenses.autonomous: The nightly AFAS refresh builds the ageing, flags customers over limit or past a set age and drafts a one-line reason from collection notes; stop-supply and provisions wait for the director.
lenses.ambitious: A decision made far more often: a weekly cash-in forecast per customer for 30 to 60 days ahead, which treasury and the bank would want more of as it gets cheaper.
lenses.joy: Nobody misses the weekly Excel rebuild; the director wants more time on the few customer conversations that actually move cash.
lenses.options: Little; the choice is mostly escalate or wait per customer, so extra drafts add effort without changing much.
lenses.altitude: The director sets the collection rules and escalation thresholds and watches DSO trend instead of balances; somewhat more expert, less clerical.
reach: Take over the weekly ageing review from the Credit and Collections Officer's manager role; needs knowledge of dispute causes in transport (PODs, damage claims)

tasks.human_edge: Knowing when pushing a key shipper for payment hurts the relationship more than the late cash, and negotiating it.
tasks.pattern_why: Ageing buckets, limits and thresholds can be written as rules; a light model step only summarises notes.

in_practice.trigger: Nightly AFAS extract; weekly Monday report.
steps: Compute ageing, DSO and over-limit flags in Power BI
Pull dispute notes and summarise the reason per top-20 customer
Send exception list to director and collections officer
Director decides escalations and provisions
in_practice.human_gate: Director approves stop-supply, write-off and provisions; routine reminders run without review.
in_practice.logs_to: Power BI history and AFAS collection notes.

evidence.claim: 81% of Dutch finance professionals explain DSO after the fact; only 12% plan cash-in beyond 30 days.
Ageing and DSO dashboards on ERP open items are routine BI work.

risks: Dispute notes in AFAS incomplete, so reasons are wrong
Automated pressure on small customers harming relationships
research_questions: How complete are collection notes in AFAS today?
How much of overdue balance is disputes versus slow payers?
Would a weekly cash-in forecast reduce facility drawdown?

tasks.short: Prepare the annual accounts, board reports and statutory filings: KVK, tax, and soon e-invoicing and possibly CSRD.

today.trigger: Year-end, board meetings, tax deadlines and auditor requests.
steps: Close the books in AFAS and agree adjustments with the Controller
Build the annual accounts and notes in Excel and Word
Answer the auditor's questions and process adjustments
File with KVK and the tax authority and present to the board
drudgery: Rolling forward last year's notes by hand
Rebuilding workpapers the auditor asks for
today.time_sinks: Audit adjustments and late questions, plus formatting notes and tables.

lenses.faster: Tables and roll-forward notes come from fixed mappings and a model drafts note text from changes; the director reviews and signs, saving about 40%.
lenses.autonomous: Close completion in AFAS starts table generation and a draft notes pack; filing and board submission wait for the director and auditor.
lenses.ambitious: A new service to the board: a monthly short statutory-style pack, so year-end holds fewer surprises; demand would grow mildly as it gets cheaper.
lenses.joy: Nobody misses copying notes; the director wants more time on the judgment items: provisions, going concern, disclosures.
lenses.options: Draft disclosure wordings for judgment areas help the director and auditor agree faster, and can change what is disclosed.
lenses.altitude: The director owns the reporting calendar, mapping rules and a regulatory watch (SBR, e-invoicing 2030, CSRD threshold) rather than assembling documents; more expert.
reach: Absorb part of the Controller's year-end file preparation; needs to own the AFAS-to-reporting mapping

tasks.human_edge: Accounting judgments, talks with the auditor, and personal accountability for what is signed and filed.
tasks.pattern_why: Mappings from AFAS ledgers to report lines are fixed rules; one model step drafts narrative notes for review.

in_practice.trigger: Year-end close flag in AFAS or a board meeting date.
steps: Map trial balance to report lines with fixed rules
Generate tables and roll forward last year's notes
Model drafts changed note text with sources
Director and Controller review, auditor checks, then filing via SBR
in_practice.human_gate: Director signs every report and filing; nothing files automatically.
in_practice.logs_to: SharePoint audit file with workpapers the auditor can rebuild.

evidence.claim: Large companies file accounts with KVK via SBR from FY2025; AFAS cannot do this for them.
CSRD now applies above 1,000 employees and €450 million turnover.
B2B e-invoicing planned from 1 July 2030, digital reporting from 1 July 2031.

risks: Missing a new obligation if the regulatory watch is not owned
research_questions: Is Noordhaven's turnover above €450 million, putting it in CSRD scope?
How many audit adjustments last year came from manual errors?
Will the auditor accept generated workpapers?

tasks.short: Review how finance works (systems, collection and AP procedures, controls) and propose changes.

today.trigger: Audit findings, a close that runs late, or a new system or law (e-invoicing, AI tools).
steps: Collect complaints, audit letters and process metrics
Walk through the process with the team
Write a proposal with cost and benefit
Agree with the director team and the OR where work changes
today.time_sinks: Getting facts on how the process actually runs, and documenting it.

lenses.faster: Process data (touchless invoice rate, close days, exceptions) comes from AFAS logs and AI drafts procedure documents; about 25% saved.
lenses.autonomous: Little runs alone; a quarterly control scan flags exceptions, and the director decides.
lenses.ambitious: A new service: a finance AI governance register for the director team, listing which tools and agents run, with which thresholds and logs, and demand grows as AI use spreads.
lenses.joy: Nobody misses writing procedure manuals; the director wants more time on redesigning the close and AP flows.
lenses.options: Two or three process designs (e.g. AP with or without Peppol-first) change the investment decision.
lenses.altitude: The director becomes owner of the finance control system: which agents, which thresholds, which logs, who signs; clearly more expert.
reach: Absorb system choices from IT for finance tools; needs basic knowledge of AFAS configuration and AI tool governance

tasks.human_edge: Weighing team capacity, works council concerns and audit risk, and getting people to change how they work.
tasks.pattern_why: The director leads the evaluation; AI gathers metrics and drafts documents.

in_practice.trigger: Quarterly control review or an audit finding.
steps: Pull process metrics from AFAS and Power BI
AI drafts current-state description and options
Director tests options with the team
Proposal to director team and OR if needed
in_practice.human_gate: Director decides; OR consulted on changes to work.

evidence.claim: Shadow AI in accounting: figures in personal chatbots and unrebuildable workpapers; provide an approved tool rather than only block.
66% of CFOs report central AI controls against 45% of managers.
AFAS Profit sends and receives Peppol but is not Peppol-first.

risks: Controls written but not followed on the floor
AI switched on by vendor updates without review
research_questions: Which AI tools does the finance team already use, approved or not?
What is today's touchless invoice rate in AFAS?
Does the OR need to be consulted on AI tools in finance (WOR art. 27)?

tasks.short: Make the monthly operational and risk reports for the director team: margins, flex costs, cash, risks.

steps: Export figures from AFAS and Power BI
Add agency hours and invoice data
Build slides in PowerPoint with commentary
Present and take follow-up questions
today.time_sinks: Combining agency portal data with AFAS and writing commentary.

lenses.faster: Fixed dashboard pages and model-drafted commentary replace slide building; director edits, about 50% saved.
lenses.autonomous: Close completion triggers the pack and draft commentary; the director approves before it goes out.
lenses.ambitious: A group served for the first time: site managers in Tilburg and Venlo get a monthly one-page margin and flex-cost report for their own site, and demand will grow, so cap the volume.
lenses.joy: Nobody misses slide formatting; the director wants more time on the risks discussion.
lenses.options: Little; one clear report beats several drafts.
lenses.altitude: The director chooses which risks and KPIs are reported and caps the number of reports; somewhat more expert.
reach: Absorb the FP&A Analyst's monthly pack build; needs Power BI ownership

tasks.human_edge: Choosing what the director team must hear, including bad news, and framing it.
tasks.pattern_why: Numbers come from fixed dashboards; one model call drafts commentary that the director checks.

steps: Refresh Power BI pages incl. agency hours
Model drafts commentary per page
Director edits and approves
Publish to Teams and SharePoint

evidence.claim: Executive reporting takes about 32 hours a month and more for AI-mature teams; cap volume.
Workday's Accounting Agent prepares work while teams stay responsible for review and decisions.

risks: Report count grows and saved time returns
Agency portal data not matched to AFAS
research_questions: Can the three agency portals export hours in a usable format?
Which current reports does the director team actually read?
How long does the pack take today, measured?

tasks.short: Use cost data to build next year's budget: wages under the CAO, flex workers, fuel, sites.

today.trigger: Annual budget cycle in autumn and mid-year reviews.
steps: Collect cost history from AFAS
Apply CAO wage increases and headcount plans
Estimate flex-worker volumes and agency rates per season
Agree budgets with site managers
today.time_sinks: Back-and-forth with site managers on versions of Excel templates.

lenses.faster: A driver-based model fills history and CAO rates automatically and AI explains changes; about 35% saved.
lenses.autonomous: Little; the model recalculates on input changes, the director decides.
lenses.ambitious: A decision made far more often: re-budget flex-worker spend monthly against volumes instead of once a year.
lenses.joy: Nobody misses merging templates; the director wants more time on choices with site managers.
lenses.options: Scenarios on flex share, CAO outcome and fuel change the budget decision itself.
lenses.altitude: The director sets the drivers and assumptions rather than collecting numbers; more expert.
reach: Absorb part of the FP&A Analyst's budget consolidation; needs driver-based modelling skills

tasks.human_edge: Negotiating budgets with site managers and weighing trade-offs between sites.
tasks.pattern_why: Budgeting is a negotiated judgment; AI supports scenarios and data.

steps: Load cost history and CAO rates
Build scenarios
Director reviews with site managers
Final budget into AFAS
in_practice.human_gate: Director and director team approve the budget.

evidence.claim: Driver-based budget scenarios in Excel or planning tools are routine practice.
Data quality is the top barrier to finance AI (40.4%).

research_questions: How accurate were last year's flex-worker budgets per site?
Can agency rates be loaded automatically?
Would monthly re-budgeting change decisions?

tasks.short: Follow fuel prices, interest rates and currency to judge cost exposure and hedging.

today.trigger: Monthly review or a sharp move in diesel or interest rates.
steps: Read market reports and bank updates
Compare with fuel cost and facility rate in AFAS
Estimate impact on margin
Decide on fuel surcharges or hedges
today.time_sinks: Collecting prices and linking them to own exposure.

lenses.faster: A monthly brief with prices, exposure and margin impact is generated; the director reads and decides, about 55% saved.
lenses.autonomous: A price feed update triggers the exposure calculation and brief; hedging and surcharge choices stay with the director.
lenses.ambitious: A new service to sales: an updated fuel surcharge proposal per customer contract each month, which sales would want more of.
lenses.joy: Nobody misses copying prices; the director wants more time on surcharge and hedging decisions.
lenses.options: Scenarios on diesel and rates change the hedge or surcharge decision.
lenses.altitude: The director owns the exposure policy and limits; more expert.
reach: Absorb fuel surcharge calculations from sales support; needs contract clause knowledge

tasks.human_edge: Deciding to hedge or pass costs on, and talking to the bank and customers.
tasks.pattern_why: Fixed calculation of exposure plus one model call to write the brief.

in_practice.trigger: Monthly or price move above threshold.
steps: Load prices and own volumes
Calculate exposure
Model drafts brief
Director decides
in_practice.human_gate: Director approves any hedge or surcharge change.

evidence.claim: At Noordhaven 'securities' means fuel, interest and currency exposure.
Cash allocation and strategic purchases need mandatory human review.

risks: Brief taken as advice without review
research_questions: How large is fuel cost exposure versus margin?
Do customer contracts have fuel clauses?
Is a reliable price feed available?

role.altitude: From building and approving reports to owning Noordhaven's finance control system: which tools and agents run, at what thresholds, with which logs, and who signs.
reach: FP&A Analyst: monthly reforecast and management pack build
Credit and Collections Officer: first-line credit limit proposals and weekly ageing review
Controller: year-end file preparation and reporting mappings
IT: choice and governance of finance AI tools
role.ceiling_note: Bounded by accountability: credit approval, statutory sign-off, bank and board relations and hedging decisions stay human; perhaps 25-35% of hours freed, partly eaten by more reporting unless volume is capped.
skills_to_grow: AI governance and EU AI Act duties for credit scoring
Process design for touchless AP and e-invoicing
Data quality ownership of the AFAS extract
role.ambitious_version: Run a weekly 13-week cash and margin forecast per site, quarterly credit limit reviews for all customers, and a governed register of finance AI agents, cutting close days and DSO while the board trusts the forecast.
